Office Notes, Office Memoranda of Court's or Judge's Coram, appearances, Court's Orders or directions and Registrar's order_____________________________________________________  Shri M.G. Bhangade, Senior Advocate a/w Shri A  Advocate for the petitioners
Shri A.S. Fulzele, APP for the respondents/Sta  CORAM : SUNIL B. SHUKRE AND  AVINASH G. GHAROTE, JJ.
DATED : 23/11/2020 Heard this matter for sometime.

During the course of hearing, Shri M.G.
Bhangade, ld.

Senior Counsel for the petitioners invited our attention to various provisions made under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short the "Act of 2006"), which are of extreme importance for the purpose of adjudicating upon the issues involved in this petition.

On going through these provisions, in particular those contained under Sections 42 and 47 of the Act of 2006,
prima facie, we find that an elaborate procedure has been prescribed for launching prosecution and prima facie, it appears to us that without there being report given by Food Analyst regarding the food item in question, and the report showing the prima facie violation of various responsibilities and duties as prescribed under Section 26 CrWP 543.2020.odt of the Act of 2006, no prosecution could be launched.

We also further prima facie find that when there is separate mechanism prescribed for launching of prosecution, the action of registration of the FIR at least for the offence punishable under the provisions of the said Act may not be justifiable.

As regards the IPC offences which have been registered against the petitioner, prima facie, we find that even for these offences,
some expert's opinion would be necessary.
Today, the Food Safety Officer is personally present in the Court and he submits that the report of the Food Analyst is still awaited.

According to him,
sample of the food in question in the present case was taken on 06.10.2020, which was Tuesday and it was sent for analysis and report on 07.10.2020, the succeeding working day.

Under Section 42(2)

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From the own submission of Food Safety Officer, it appears at this juncture that there is a prima facie violation of the requirement of Section 42(2) of the Act of 2006 in the present case.
Learned Senior Counsel Shri M.G. Bhangade has pointed out to us many more such violations.

However, learned APP Shri Fulzele, appearing for the respondents/State submits that on certain aspects of the matter his instructions are still awaited and, therefore, he seeks further one week's time by way of last chance.

Learned Senior Advocate Shri M.G. Bhangade submits that CrWP 543.2020.odt if further time is to be granted, at least the Food Safety Officer be directed to release the seized goods to the custody of the petitioners, who is also a food business operator, being a transporter, as required under Section 38 of the Act of 2006.
Since, we would be dealing with all the issues involved in this case and deciding the same finally, we do not think it necessary to pass any interim order at this stage.
Accordingly, matter is posted for final hearing at the admission stage on 27.11.2020.
The respondents may file their affidavit-in-reply latest by 26.11.2020 and if such affidavit is filed, it's copy be furnished in advance to the petitioners or the learned Senior Counsel.
S.O. to 27.11.2020, at the end of the Board.

Physical hearing is allowed, subject to convenience of the parties.
